# Proverbs 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Don't be jealous of people who do evil, and don't wish you could be part of their circle,

**2** Because their minds are set on destruction and their words stir up trouble.

**3** A home is built by wisdom and made strong by understanding;

**4** Its rooms are filled through knowledge — with every kind of beautiful and valuable thing.

**5** A wise person has more real power than a strong one, and knowledge makes strength even greater,

**6** Because strategic thinking wins wars, and having plenty of advisors leads to victory.

**7** Real wisdom is beyond a fool's reach — they have nothing to say when important decisions are being made.

**8** A person who spends their time scheming will be known as a troublemaker.

**9** The plans of a fool are sinful, and people despise a mocker.

**10** If you collapse under pressure, your strength was never real.

**11** Rescue people who are being dragged toward death. Hold back those who are staggering toward execution.

**12** If you say, 'We didn't know about this' — the God who examines hearts will see through that excuse. He watches over your life and will repay you according to what you've done.

**13** My child, eat honey — it's good for you! The fresh honeycomb is sweet on your tongue.

**14** That's what wisdom does for your soul — find it, and you have a future. Your hope won't be disappointed.

**15** Don't plot against an innocent person's home. Don't try to destroy where they live.

**16** A righteous person may fall seven times but gets up every time. The wicked, though, go down and stay down.

**17** Don't celebrate when your enemy falls, and don't let your heart be happy when they stumble,

**18** Because the LORD might see your attitude and disapprove — and then redirect His judgment away from them.

**19** Don't obsess over evil people or envy the wicked,

**20** Because bad people have no future — their light will be snuffed out.

**21** My child, respect the LORD and respect authority. Don't associate with people who stir up rebellion,

**22** Because their disaster will come without warning, and who knows what destruction both God and the king can bring?

**23** Here are more sayings from the wise: showing favoritism in court is wrong.

**24** Anyone who tells a guilty person, 'You're innocent,' will be cursed by whole communities and despised by nations.

**25** But those who have the courage to confront wrongdoing will be appreciated, and good things will come their way.

**26** An honest, straightforward answer is as welcome as a kiss on the lips.

**27** Get your outdoor work done first — prepare your fields — and then build your house.

**28** Don't testify against your neighbor without good reason, and don't lie about them.

**29** Don't say, 'I'll do to them exactly what they did to me — I'll pay them back for what they've done.'

**30** I once walked past a lazy person's field and the vineyard of someone with no sense,

**31** And the whole place was overrun with weeds. Thorns covered everything, and the stone wall had collapsed.

**32** I looked at it, thought about it, and learned a lesson:

**33** A little more sleep, a little more rest, a little more folding of the hands —

**34** And poverty will mug you, and need will attack you like an armed robber.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **24:10**: Short and devastating — pressure reveals the truth about your character. If you crumble when things get hard, your strength was never real.

- **24:16**: This isn't about falling into sin — it's about resilience. Good people get knocked down constantly. What makes them righteous is that they always get up.

- **24:30-34**: A brilliant little parable — the teacher walks past a ruined field and extracts a lesson. Laziness is its own destruction. You don't even need an enemy; neglect does the job.

— PNEUMA
